newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- outperforms, down about 1 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- outperforms, down about 1 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices outperformed Treasuries Friday, as traders counted themselves lucky to have lost slightly more than a point on the bid side.
"Bids are down 1-1/4, but it's not as bad as Treasuries," one trader said. The government long bond lost more than two points on the day.

Friday's freefall began after the National Association of Purchasing Management's July report sent an inflation scare through the market at mid-morning. It jolted investors already unnerved by a strong employment report earlier in the day.

The NAPM survey's headline diffusion index showed a sharp rise, moving to 58.6 percent in July from 55.7 percent in June, the highest reading since November 1994. The price component also jumped significantly, another indication of rising price pressure.

The Treasury market, which sold off modestly after the stronger-than-expected July employment report, went into a sharp decline falling NAPM. The government long bond continued to fall throughout the afternoon, dropping 2-5/32 points and driving the yield to 6.46 percent from 6.30 percent at the close on Thursday.

Futures markets also sold off sharply, as the September municipal contract lost 1-21/32 to 120-16/32 and September T-bonds dropped 1-30/32 to 114-26/32. The MOB spread widened to 182 ticks from 173 at the close on Thursday.
Actively traded secondary market issues included Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5.0s of 2024, which were bid at 5.42 percent, up 10 basis points.
Next week's new deals were expected to total $3.9 billion in 111 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totalled $2.8 billion in 49 sales, with a $464 million Allegheny County Airport, Pa., offering through Morgan Stanley & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 62 sales totaling $1.1 billion were scheduled. A $240 million Georgia offering on Tuesday was the largest.
